ing: or chicken broth with 2 tbsp red wine vinegar
st: Pat the chicken dry and season it with [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Cook the bacon in a large heavy pot over medium heat for 6 minutes until crisp. Lift it out and leave the fat in the pot.
Brown the chicken in the bacon fat in batches, skin side down first, about 5 minutes per side. Move it to a plate.
Add [[1 tbsp]] butter, the onion, and the mushrooms to the pot. Cook for 8 minutes until golden, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Sprinkle in [[2 tbsp]] flour and stir for 1 minute. Pour in [[3 cups]] wine and scrape up the browned bits.
Add [[1 cup]] chicken broth, the thyme, the bay leaf, the bacon, and the chicken with its juices.
Bring to a simmer, cover partly, and cook on low for 50 minutes until the chicken is tender and reaches at least 165°F (74°C).
Take out the chicken and boil the sauce for 10 minutes to thicken. Whisk in the last [[1 tbsp]] butter and discard the herbs.
Return the chicken to the sauce and serve with mashed potatoes or bread.

ing: Burgundy style, or beef broth with 2 tbsp red wine vinegar
st: Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Pat the beef very dry and toss it with [[2 tsp]] salt, [[1 tsp]] pepper, and [[3 tbsp]] flour.
Cook the bacon in a large oven-safe pot for 6 minutes until crisp. Remove it and keep the fat.
Add [[2 tbsp]] oil and brown the beef in batches over medium-high heat, 2 minutes per side. Do not crowd the pot. Set aside.
Cook the onion and carrots in the pot for 6 minutes. Stir in [[3 cloves]] garlic and [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste for 1 minute.
Pour in [[3 cups]] wine and scrape up the browned bits. Boil for 3 minutes.
Add the beef, bacon, [[1.5 cups]] broth, and thyme. Bring to a simmer, cover, and move to the oven.
Cook for 2 hours, until the beef is nearly tender.
Stir in the mushrooms and cook 30 minutes more, uncovered, so the sauce thickens.
Taste, adjust the salt, remove the thyme stems, and serve with potatoes or noodles.
Toss the eggplant cubes with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and let them sit in a colander for 15 minutes. Pat dry.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Cook the eggplant for 8 minutes until golden. Remove to a plate.
Add another [[2 tbsp]] oil and cook the zucchini for 5 minutes until lightly browned. Add to the plate.
Add the last [[1 tbsp]] oil, the onion, and the pepper. Cook for 8 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, thyme, [[1 tsp]] salt, and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes until juicy.
Return the eggplant and zucchini to the pot and stir gently.
Cover and cook on low for 20 minutes, then uncover and cook 10 minutes more to thicken.
Remove the thyme stems, stir in the basil, and serve warm or at room temperature.
Melt [[3 tbsp]] butter with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onions and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Cook, stirring every few minutes, for 45 minutes until the onions are deep golden brown. Lower the heat if they scorch.
Pour in [[0.5 cup]] wine and scrape the bottom of the pot until the liquid mostly evaporates.
Add [[6 cups]] beef broth, the thyme, the bay leaf, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the broiler. Toast the bread slices on a tray for 2 minutes per side.
Remove the thyme and bay leaf and taste the soup for salt.
Ladle soup into oven-safe bowls on a baking sheet. Top each with 2 bread slices and [[1.5 oz]] grated cheese.
Broil for 3 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and browned. Let cool for a few minutes before eating.
Cover the beans with water by 2 inches and soak overnight, or boil for 2 minutes and soak for 1 hour. Drain and rinse.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Season the duck and pork with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Brown the duck legs skin side down in a large oven-safe pot for 8 minutes. Remove, pour off all but 2 tablespoons of fat.
Brown the pork cubes and sausages in the pot for 8 minutes. Remove and slice the sausages.
Cook the bacon and onion for 6 minutes, add the garlic for 1 minute, then stir in the tomatoes.
Add the beans, [[3 cups]] broth, thyme, bay leaves, [[1 tsp]] salt, and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Tuck in the pork and duck.
Cover and bake for 90 minutes. Stir in the sliced sausage, push the duck skin side up, and add water if dry.
Sprinkle with [[0.5 cup]] breadcrumbs and bake uncovered for 60 minutes until a crust forms and the beans are very tender.
Rest 15 minutes, check that the pork is at least 145°F (63°C), and serve.

ing: such as cod or halibut, in chunks
or clam juice mixed with water
st: Heat [[0.25 cup]] olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and fennel and cook for 10 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, orange zest, and bay leaf for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes. Cook for 8 minutes.
Crumble the saffron into [[0.5 cup]] of the warm stock and let it steep for 5 minutes.
Pour the saffron liquid and the remaining stock into the pot. Add [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the fish chunks and simmer gently for 4 minutes.
Add the mussels and shrimp, cover, and cook for 4 minutes until the mussels open and the shrimp are pink. Discard any unopened mussels.
Remove the bay leaf and taste for salt.
Serve in wide bowls with toasted baguette slices.
Mix [[1.25 cups]] flour and [[0.25 tsp]] salt. Rub in [[0.5 cup]] cold butter with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] ice water until the dough holds together. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Roll the dough into a 12-inch circle and press it into a 9-inch tart pan.
Line the dough with parchment and fill with dry beans. Bake for 15 minutes, remove the parchment, and bake 5 minutes more.
Cook the bacon for 8 minutes until crisp, then drain on paper towels.
Lower the oven to 350°F (175°C). Whisk the eggs, [[1 cup]] cream, [[0.5 cup]] milk, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Scatter the bacon and [[1 cup]] cheese into the crust and pour in the custard.
Bake for 35 minutes until set with a slight wobble in the center and the center reads 160°F (71°C).
Cool for 15 minutes before slicing.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Melt [[1 tbsp]] butter in a small pan over medium heat. Whisk in [[2 tbsp]] flour and cook for 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in [[1 cup]] warm milk, the nutmeg, and [[0.25 tsp]] salt. Simmer for 3 minutes until thick, then stir in [[0.5 cup]] cheese.
Spread mustard on 4 bread slices. Top each with 2 slices ham, [[0.25 cup]] cheese, and a second bread slice.
Melt the remaining [[2 tbsp]] butter and brush it on the outsides of the sandwiches.
Toast the sandwiches on the baking sheet for 5 minutes per side until golden.
Spread the sauce over the tops and sprinkle with the remaining [[0.5 cup]] cheese.
Bake or broil for 4 minutes until bubbling and browned, then serve hot.

ing: beaten with 1 tbsp milk for wash
st: Mix [[3.5 cups]] flour, [[0.25 cup]] sugar, [[2 tsp]] salt, and [[2.25 tsp]] yeast. Add [[0.75 cup]] warm milk and [[0.25 cup]] warm water. Knead for 5 minutes into a smooth dough.
Wrap the dough and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Shape the cold butter into a 6-inch square between parchment sheets. Chill it.
Roll the dough into a 12-inch square. Put the butter on it like a diamond, fold the corners over, and pinch the seams shut.
Roll into a long rectangle about 20 by 8 inches. Fold in thirds like a letter, wrap, and chill for 45 minutes.
Repeat the roll, fold, and chill two more times. If butter leaks, dust it with flour.
Roll the dough into a 20 by 12 inch rectangle, cut into 8 triangles, and roll each from the wide end to the tip.
Place on lined trays, cover, and rise at room temperature for 90 minutes until puffy.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush with the egg wash.
Bake for 18 minutes until deep golden. Cool for 10 minutes before eating.
Stir [[3.5 cups]] flour, [[1 tsp]] yeast, and [[2 tsp]] salt in a large bowl. Add [[1.25 cups]] warm water and mix into a shaggy dough.
Knead on a floured counter for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Put the dough in an oiled bowl, cover, and let it rise for 90 minutes until doubled.
Divide the dough into 2 pieces. Flatten each into a rectangle, fold it in thirds, and let it rest for 15 minutes.
Roll each piece into a 15-inch log, sealing the seam, and place on a floured towel or baguette pan.
Cover and let rise for 45 minutes. Heat the oven with a baking stone or sheet inside to 475°F (245°C) and put an empty pan on the bottom rack.
Slash each loaf 4 times on the diagonal with a sharp blade.
Slide the loaves in and drop the ice cubes into the hot pan for steam.
Bake for 25 minutes until deep golden brown. Cool on a rack for 20 minutes.

ing: melted, plus extra for the pan
st: Whisk [[1 cup]] flour, [[1 tbsp]] sugar, and [[0.25 tsp]] salt in a bowl.
Add the eggs and [[0.5 cup]] of the milk and whisk until smooth.
Whisk in the remaining [[0.75 cup]] milk and [[2 tbsp]] melted butter until the batter is thin like cream.
Rest the batter for 30 minutes in the fridge so it relaxes.
Heat a 10-inch nonstick pan over medium heat and brush lightly with butter.
Pour in about [[0.25 cup]] batter and swirl to coat the pan. Cook for 1 minute until the edges lift.
Flip and cook 30 seconds more. Slide onto a plate and repeat, buttering the pan as needed.
Serve warm with lemon juice and powdered sugar, folded into quarters.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Set six 6-oz ramekins in a deep baking dish.
Warm [[2 cups]] cream in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming, not boiling. Stir in [[1 tbsp]] vanilla.
Whisk the yolks, [[0.25 cup]] sugar, and the salt in a bowl until pale.
Slowly pour the hot cream into the yolks while whisking so the eggs do not scramble.
Strain the custard and divide it among the ramekins.
Pour [[4 cups]] hot water into the dish around the ramekins, halfway up their sides.
Bake for 35 minutes until set at the edges with a slight wobble in the center.
Cool, then chill for at least 4 hours.
Sprinkle the remaining [[0.25 cup]] sugar on top and caramelize with a kitchen torch, or broil for 2 minutes. Let it harden for 2 minutes.
Combine the shallot, [[0.25 cup]] vinegar, [[2 tbsp]] wine, crushed peppercorns, and [[1 tbsp]] tarragon in a small pan.
Simmer over medium heat for 6 minutes until only about 2 tablespoons of liquid remain. Strain and cool for 5 minutes.
Set a heatproof bowl over a pan of barely simmering water. The bowl must not touch the water.
Whisk the yolks with the reduction in the bowl for 4 minutes until thick, pale, and ribbons trail off the whisk. Do not let it scramble.
Remove from the heat and add [[0.75 cup]] warm melted butter a few drops at a time, whisking, then in a thin stream.
Stir in the remaining [[1 tbsp]] tarragon and [[0.25 tsp]] salt. The yolks are gently cooked here, so serve right away.
Thin with a teaspoon of warm water if too thick. Serve warm over steak.
Melt [[0.75 cup]] butter and keep it warm.
Fill a small pan with 1 inch of water and bring to a bare simmer.
Whisk the yolks with [[1 tbsp]] water in a heatproof bowl until frothy.
Set the bowl over the pan, not touching the water, and whisk for 3 minutes until thick and pale and the eggs reach about 160°F (71°C).
Take the bowl off the heat. Slowly drizzle in the warm butter, whisking all the time, to build a smooth emulsion.
Whisk in [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice, [[0.25 tsp]] salt, and the cayenne.
If the sauce is too thick, whisk in a few drops of warm water. Serve at once over eggs or vegetables.
Take the cheeses and pâté out of the fridge 30 minutes before serving so they lose their chill and show their full flavor. Leave the wrapping on until you plate.
Peel the casing from the saucisson, then slice it into rounds about 1/8 inch thick. Fan the slices in an overlapping line along one edge of a large wooden board.
Fold the ham slices loosely in half, then in half again, and pile them in a soft mound next to the saucisson so the board has height.
Slice the pâté into 1/2 inch slabs, or set the crock on the board with a small knife. Cut the Comté into thin slabs and the Roquefort into rough crumbly wedges.
Set the Brie whole with one wedge already cut out, so guests see how to start. Keep the three cheeses apart so the Roquefort does not flavor the rest.
Slice the baguette on the bias into 1/2 inch pieces and set them in a basket or at the open end of the board. Put the butter in a small dish.
Spoon the cornichons and [[3 tbsp]] mustard into two small bowls and tuck them between the meats. Fill the gaps with the grapes. Serve right away.
nt: Don't cook: slice, fold, arrange; cheeses at room temperature 30 minutes
Best swap: Cantal or Gruyère for Comté, rillettes for the pâté; for vegetarians skip the meats and add a marinated mushroom pâté.

ing: pitted, or leave pits in for tradition
st: Heat the oven to 375°F. Grease a 9 inch baking dish with [[1 tbsp]] butter and sprinkle with a little sugar.
Spread [[3 cups]] pitted cherries in the dish in a single layer.
Whisk the 3 eggs with [[0.5 cup]] sugar until pale, about 2 minutes. Whisk in [[0.5 cup]] flour and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Whisk in [[1 cup]] milk, [[0.5 cup]] cream and [[1 tsp]] vanilla. The batter should be thin like crepe batter.
Rest the batter for 10 minutes, then pour it gently over the cherries.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes until puffed, golden and a knife in the center comes out clean (the eggs are fully cooked).
Cool 15 minutes; it will sink slightly. Dust with [[1 tbsp]] sugar and serve warm.
nt: Baked at 375°F
Best swap: plums, apricots or frozen cherries (thawed and drained) for fresh cherries in the same amount.

st: Heat the oven to 400°F. Melt the butter in a 10 inch oven-safe skillet over medium heat, then sprinkle in the sugar and salt.
Cook without stirring for 6 to 8 minutes until the sugar turns deep amber, swirling the pan. Take care, hot caramel burns badly.
Take the pan off the heat. Pack in the apple halves, rounded side down, in tight circles. Stir the vanilla over them.
Return to medium heat and cook for 10 minutes until the apples soften and the juices bubble thickly.
Roll the pastry slightly bigger than the pan and lay it over the apples, tucking the edges down inside the rim. Cut 3 small steam slits.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the pastry is puffed and deep golden.
Rest the tart for 10 minutes, then run a knife round the edge, put a plate over the pan and flip it with oven gloves in one quick move.
nt: Pan-caramelized, then baked at 400°F
Best swap: use firm pears in place of apples 1 to 1, or a shortcrust dough in place of puff pastry.

st: Line an 8 inch square pan with wafer paper. Warm the almonds and pistachios in a 300°F oven for 10 minutes and keep them warm.
Cook the honey in a small pot to 250°F, about 8 minutes, stirring now and then.
In another pot boil the sugar, corn syrup and water to 300°F, about 12 minutes, without stirring.
Whip the pasteurized egg whites to stiff peaks. Pour in the honey in a thin stream while whipping on medium for 3 minutes.
Slowly add the hot sugar syrup, still whipping, then whip about 5 minutes until the mix is thick and holds a trail.
Fold in the warm nuts quickly with an oiled spatula, press into the pan, top with wafer paper and weigh down. Rest 6 hours, then cut.
nt: Cooked syrups, whipped, no baking
Best swap: use all honey in place of the corn syrup for a softer bite, or dried cranberries for half the pistachios.

st: Mix the flour, milk, yeast, sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt into a soft dough. Chill 1 hour wrapped.
Pound the cold butter between parchment into a 6 inch square about 1/2 inch thick. Roll the dough to a 9 inch square and wrap around the butter like an envelope, pinching the seams.
Roll into a 8 by 20 inch strip, fold in thirds like a letter, wrap and chill 30 minutes.
Roll and fold in thirds again twice more, chilling 30 minutes after each fold, for three folds in total.
Roll to 8 by 20 inch rectangle, 1/4 inch thick. Cut into 8 rectangles, place 2 chocolate batons on each, and roll up with the seam underneath.
Place on lined trays, cover and rise 1 hour until puffy. Heat the oven to 400°F.
Brush with the egg and bake 16 to 20 minutes until deep golden brown. Cool 10 minutes.
nt: Baked at 400°F
Best swap: use 3 oz chopped bittersweet chocolate instead of batons, or plant-based block butter for dairy-free layers.

st: Boil the eggs in water for 10 minutes until the yolks are fully set, then chill in cold water and peel. Cut in quarters.
Boil the potatoes, if using, for 15 minutes until tender, then slice.
Boil the green beans in well-salted water for 4 minutes until bright green and just tender, then chill in ice water and drain.
Whisk [[1 tbsp]] vinegar, [[1 tsp]] Dijon and salt, then whisk in [[4 tbsp]] olive oil.
Arrange the tomatoes, beans and potatoes on a wide platter and toss lightly with half the dressing.
Top with the tuna in chunks, the egg quarters, the anchovies and the olives. Drizzle with the remaining dressing and serve.
nt: Boiled eggs and beans, otherwise don't cook
Best swap: seared fresh tuna steak, cooked through to 145°F, in place of the canned tuna.

st: Warm [[1 tbsp]] olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the carrots, potatoes and tomatoes and cook 5 minutes, stirring.
Pour in the water, add salt, and bring to a boil. Lower the heat and simmer for 15 minutes until the vegetables begin to soften.
Add the green beans, zucchini and white beans. Simmer another 10 minutes.
Stir in the pasta and cook 8 to 10 minutes until just tender, adding a splash of water if the soup gets too thick.
Meanwhile make the pistou. Pound or pulse the basil, garlic and a pinch of salt to a paste, then mix in the parmesan and the remaining olive oil.
Take the soup off the heat. Stir in half the pistou, then serve with a spoonful of the rest on top of each bowl.
nt: Simmered vegetable soup with raw basil paste
Best swap: skip the parmesan and add 2 tbsp toasted pine nuts or a splash more oil for a dairy-free pistou.

st: Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon and salt in a wide shallow dish until no streaks of egg remain.
Soak the bread slices in the custard for 30 seconds per side. Stale bread should feel heavy but not fall apart. Fresh bread needs only 15 seconds.
Melt [[1 tbsp]] butter in a large skillet over medium-low heat until foaming but not browning.
Fry 2 or 3 slices at a time for 3 minutes per side, until deep golden and the center feels set. Lower the heat if the outside darkens too fast.
Wipe the pan, add more butter and repeat with the remaining slices. Keep finished slices on a rack in a 200°F oven.
Dust with the powdered sugar and serve hot with the berries. The center should reach 160°F so the egg is cooked through.
nt: Pan-fried in butter
Best swap: use oat milk and coconut oil for a dairy-free version, or bake the soaked slices at 400°F for 15 minutes for a hands-off oven batch.

st: Heat the oven to 400°F. Place each pastry sheet between two baking trays lined with parchment so it bakes flat. Bake for 25 minutes.
Remove the top tray and bake 5 more minutes until deep golden and crisp. Cool completely.
Heat the milk with the vanilla bean until steaming. Do not boil.
Whisk the yolks, [[0.5 cup]] sugar and cornstarch until pale, then slowly whisk in the hot milk.
Return to the pot and cook over medium heat, whisking nonstop, for 4 minutes until thick and bubbling. Cook it to at least 160°F.
Off the heat, whisk in [[2 tbsp]] butter. Press plastic wrap on the surface and chill for 2 hours.
Trim the pastry into 18 equal rectangles. Mix the powdered sugar with [[2 tbsp]] water into a thick icing and spread it on 6 of them.
Pipe a thin line of melted chocolate across the icing and drag a toothpick through it to make a pattern.
Layer plain rectangle, cream, plain rectangle, cream, then an iced one on top. Chill 30 minutes before serving.
nt: Baked at 400°F, then assembled with chilled cream
Best swap: store-bought pastry cream or whipped cream stabilized with 1 tbsp powdered sugar per cup.

st: Heat the oven to 425°F. Line two 10 by 15 inch baking sheets with parchment.
Beat the almond flour, powdered sugar and 3 whole eggs for 5 minutes until thick and pale. Fold in the flour.
Whip the 3 whites with [[0.25 cup]] sugar to stiff peaks and fold into the batter. Split between the pans and spread level.
Bake for 7 minutes until springy and light gold. Cool, then trim each sponge and cut into 3 equal rectangles.
Boil [[0.5 cup]] water and [[0.5 cup]] sugar for 2 minutes. Cool, then stir in the coffee. This is the soaking syrup.
For the buttercream, whisk the yolks and [[0.25 cup]] syrup over a pan of simmering water to 160°F. Whip until cool and thick, then beat in the butter a bit at a time.
Heat the cream until steaming and pour over the chocolate. Wait 2 minutes and stir to a smooth ganache. Cool until spreadable.
Layer a sponge, brush with syrup, spread buttercream, add a sponge, syrup, ganache, then repeat to build six layers. Chill 1 hour.
Pour the remaining ganache over the top, smooth it and chill until set. Trim the edges with a hot knife for clean slices.
nt: Baked at 425°F, then layered and chilled
Best swap: strong brewed tea or espresso diluted with water in place of the coffee syrup.

st: Toss the strawberries with the sugar and lemon juice in a bowl and leave for 1 hour until syrupy.
Put a small plate in the freezer to test the set later.
Pour everything into a wide heavy pot and bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring.
Skim off the foam and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick and glossy.
Spoon a drop of jam onto the cold plate. After 1 minute push it with a finger. If it wrinkles, it is set. If not, cook 3 minutes more.
Ladle into clean jars, cap and cool. Keeps 3 weeks in the fridge.
nt: Macerated, then simmered until set
Best swap: raspberries or apricots at the same weight, and cut the sugar to 1 cup if the fruit is sweet.

st: Heat the oven to 375°F. Line a 10 by 15 inch jelly roll pan with parchment and grease it lightly. Whisk the flour, cocoa and salt together.
Beat the egg yolks with [[0.5 cup]] sugar for 4 minutes until pale and thick. Stir in the vanilla.

In a clean bowl, whip the egg whites to soft peaks, then add the remaining [[0.25 cup]] sugar and whip to stiff glossy peaks. Fold a third of the whites into the yolks, then fold in the rest and the dry mix gently.

Spread the batter evenly in the pan and bake 10 to 12 minutes until it springs back when pressed. Turn it out onto a towel dusted with powdered sugar, peel off the parchment and roll up with the towel. Cool completely.
Whip [[1 cup]] cold cream with [[2 tbsp]] powdered sugar until it holds soft peaks. Unroll the cake, spread the cream over it, and roll it back up without the towel.
Heat the remaining [[1 cup]] cream until steaming, pour over the chocolate, wait 2 minutes and stir smooth. Let it cool 30 minutes until spreadable.
Cut a slice off one end at an angle and set it on the side as a branch. Cover the log with ganache, drag a fork along it to make bark, and dust with powdered sugar. Chill 1 hour before serving.
nt: Baked sponge, rolled, filled and chilled
Best swap: use 1 cup whipped mascarpone sweetened with 2 tbsp sugar in place of the whipped cream filling.

st: Pat the chicken dry and season well with salt and pepper. Dry skin browns better and does not spatter.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] olive oil in a wide Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the chicken skin side down for 6 minutes until deep golden, flip and sear 3 minutes more. Move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the ham, onion and peppers in the chicken fat for 10 minutes until soft and lightly browned at the edges.
Stir in the garlic, Espelette pepper and thyme and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in [[0.5 cup]] white wine and scrape up the browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes, then add the crushed tomatoes.
Nestle the chicken back in, skin side up. Cover and braise over low heat for 35 minutes, until the thickest piece reads 175°F and the juices run clear.
Uncover and simmer 8 minutes to thicken the sauce. Taste, adjust the salt, and serve with rice or boiled potatoes.
nt: Seared, then braised covered on the stove
Best swap: use 1 tsp smoked sweet paprika plus a pinch of cayenne in place of Espelette, and prosciutto for Bayonne ham.

st: Stir [[2 cup]] flour, [[1 tsp]] salt, [[0.75 cup]] water and [[2 tbsp]] oil into a smooth dough. Knead 5 minutes, cover and rest 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to its maximum, at least 500°F, with a baking sheet or stone inside.
Mix [[1 cup]] fromage blanc, [[0.25 cup]] cream, a pinch of nutmeg, salt and pepper into a smooth spread.
Cook the bacon in a dry skillet over medium heat for 4 minutes until it just starts to color. Drain on paper towels.
Divide the dough in 2 and roll each piece as thin as a cracker on parchment, about 12 inches across.
Spread the cream mix over each base leaving a thin rim. Top with onion slices and bacon.
Slide onto the hot sheet on the parchment and bake 8 to 10 minutes until the edges blister and char in spots. Serve right away, cut into strips.
nt: Baked at 500°F or hotter
Best swap: plain Greek yogurt thickened with 1 tbsp cream per cup works 1 to 1 for fromage blanc; skip bacon for sautéed mushrooms.

st: Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms 6 minutes until the water cooks off and they brown.
Add the shallots and chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt and the thyme. Cook 8 minutes, stirring, until the chicken is no longer pink inside.
Pour in [[0.5 cup]] cream and simmer 3 minutes until thick. Cool the filling completely, about 30 minutes, so it does not melt the pastry.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Cut one pastry sheet into a 9 inch circle and the other into a 10 inch circle. Place the smaller one on parchment.
Mound the filling on the small circle leaving a 1 inch rim. Brush the rim with egg wash and cover with the large circle, pressing the edges to seal.
Crimp the edge with a fork, brush the top with egg wash and score curved spiral lines from the center with a knife tip. Cut a small steam hole.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes until deep golden and puffed. Rest 10 minutes before slicing in wedges.
nt: Baked at 400°F
Best swap: use shortcrust dough 1 to 1 if puff pastry is unavailable, or swap the chicken for 12 oz more mushrooms for a vegetarian pie.

st: Rinse the mussels under cold water. Throw away any with cracked shells or any open ones that do not close when tapped.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the shallots and garlic for 3 minutes until soft but not colored.
Pour in the wine, add the bay leaf and bring to a boil for 1 minute.
Tip in the mussels, cover tightly and steam on high for 5 to 6 minutes, shaking the pot once or twice, until the shells open wide.
Discard any mussels that stay shut. Stir in the parsley and pepper, then ladle into bowls with the broth.
Serve with torn baguette to soak up the liquid.
nt: Steamed open in wine
Best swap: dry cider or chicken stock for the wine, same amount.

st: Heat the oven to 325°F. Rub a 9 by 13 inch baking dish with the cut garlic clove, then grease it with the [[1 tbsp]] butter.
Slice the potatoes 1/8 inch thick with a sharp knife or mandoline. Do not rinse them, the starch thickens the sauce.
In a wide pot, warm the cream, milk, minced garlic, nutmeg, [[1 tsp]] salt and pepper until steaming. Add the potato slices and simmer gently for 8 minutes, stirring often so they do not stick.
Pour the potatoes and cream into the dish and spread them flat so the top is level.
Bake for 55 to 60 minutes until the top is deep golden and a knife slides through the potatoes with no resistance.
Rest the gratin 10 minutes before serving so the cream sets slightly.
nt: Baked at 325°F
Best swap: use all whole milk plus 1 tbsp butter in place of the cream for a lighter gratin, and bake 10 minutes longer.
